_comment: Copy this file to seo-metadata.config.json in your project and fill in your own Contentful content type / field names. Nothing here is enforced by Contentful's schema — it's just telling the skill what your schema looks like. See examples/payden-and-rygel/config.json for a filled-in example.

select: seoMetadata { sys { id } title description keywords canonicalUrl schema }

rules._comment: Copy rules/*.template.md to these paths (dropping .template) and fill in your own rules. reference-data.example.json is optional — only needed if you use category/product alignment tagging. subtitleSpec is optional — set it (and contentful.seoMetadata.subtitleField) only if your SEO metadata has a Subtitle field.

canonicalUrl._comment: Canonical URL is built by `derive`, never drafted. Tokens like {slug} read from the fetched entry (dot paths; numeric segments index arrays). The first rule whose `when` path is non-empty wins; otherwise `default` is used. Remove this block if you do not manage canonical URLs.

schema._comment: JSON-LD built by `derive`. {path} reads the fetched entry, {row.x} the drafted row, {canonicalUrl} the derived URL. Filters: |date (YYYY-MM-DD), |join. A string that is a single token keeps its native type (arrays stay arrays). Anything that resolves empty is dropped. Remove this block if you do not manage schema.
